speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: The hon Member may wish to withdraw her Parliamentary Questions (PQs) if her queries are answered in today's Sitting.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: In the event that there are any supplementary questions that pertain to MOF, MHA and MAS, Sir, I seek your permission for such supplementary questions to be answered by the Ministers overseeing those Ministries and agency.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: Members periodically undergo a peer assessment, known as a "Mutual Evaluation" (ME), of their level of compliance with the FATF Standards and effectiveness of their anti money laundering, countering of terrorism financing (AML/CFT) and countering proliferation financing framework.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: Singapore was one of the first countries and the first international financial centre assessed in this fifth round of the FATF MEs.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: As with other international financial centres, business and trading hubs, Singapore is inherently exposed to transnational ML/TF/PF risks and is expected to maintain strong defences against them.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: Since the last round of MEs, higher standards have also been introduced by the FATF.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: Against this context, Singapore performed credibly and achieved better overall results than we did in the fourth round.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: Every FATF ME report, for every country, identifies both strengths and recommendations for further enhancements.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: Where the FATF has made recommendations to strengthen certain aspects of our framework, the Government will carefully study them.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: We will develop action plans that are risk-proportionate and suited to Singapore's context, ensuring that our financial and business ecosystem continues to grow in a trusted environment and create good jobs for Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: With that, let me now cover the four areas raised in the PQs.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: On international cooperation, the FATF found Singapore provides timely, quality and constructive assistance to our foreign counterparts.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: We note the feedback that some requests have taken a longer time to execute.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: This is often because further factual clarification is required or our legal requirements are not met.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: We will continue to strengthen our cooperation with foreign counterparts, including better explaining our requirements for assistance.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: This covers cooperation channels and asset recovery as well.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: Regarding BO transparency, the FATF does not prescribe a singular approach for BO transparency.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: Rather, each jurisdiction is expected to adopt measures appropriate to its own risks and context.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: The FATF then assesses whether a jurisdiction has an effective framework to ensure that accurate BO information is available to the competent authorities in a timely manner when needed.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: Against this standard, the FATF acknowledged that Singapore has taken significant steps to prevent the misuse of legal persons and legal arrangements.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: First, we have a central BO registry for all companies and Limited Liability Partnerships.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: They are required to verify the BO information periodically, while corporate service providers are also required to check on the BO of their clients as part of customer due diligence.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: The information is further validated through risk-based audits by the Accounting and Corporate Regulatory Authority.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: This is supplemented by the ownership information captured by public agencies.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: For instance, for landed residential properties, the Singapore Land Authority will conduct checks on the identity and the citizenship of the ultimate beneficial owner.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: Thus, the identity of the ultimate beneficial owner of any trust, which seeks to purchase landed residential properties, will have to be disclosed to the Government.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: Second, AML/CFT-obligated entities, such as banks, are required to conduct customer due diligence checks when dealing with their customers, which include unregistered foreign companies and trusts.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: Checks include verifying BO information, including the ultimate beneficial owner, and reporting suspicious activities.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: Third, BO information obtained by AML/CFT obligated entities is readily available to law enforcement agencies in a timely manner.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: These measures have enabled Singapore to establish an effective BO regime that supports investigations and enforcement.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: Nevertheless, we will carefully study the FATF's recommendations and consider whether further enhancements will be needed to strengthen our framework, while remaining appropriate for Singapore's risk profile.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: The FATF has acknowledged Singapore's stepped-up sanctions against FIs and VASPs for AML/CFT purposes.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: These actions are also published for deterrence and to increase industry awareness.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: MAS closely monitors the implementation and completion of FIs and VASPs' remedial measures.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: Our overall approach is effective and has led to positive behavioural changes in the industry, such as stronger compliance culture amongst FIs and VASPs and improvements in AML/CFT controls.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: These improvements have been acknowledged by the FATF.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: The FATF has recommended us to review the dissuasiveness and proportionality of our financial penalties.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: We will consider the recommendation, bearing in mind the specific details of each individual case and the range of enforcement levers available.
Countering PF and proliferation of weapons of mass destruction has been a key area of focus for Singapore.
Singapore’s FIs, such as banks and VASPs, have a good understanding of their countering proliferation financing obligations and implemented risk-based mitigation measures.
We will continue to improve our risk understanding as PF risks change and evolve.
We will also step up engagements with non-AML/CFT obligated entities to raise awareness.

Where the FATF has made recommendations to strengthen certain aspects of our framework, the Government will carefully study them and develop action plans that are risk-proportionate and suited to Singapore's context.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Allow me to first declare that I work in an FI.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Two supplementary questions for the Senior Minister of State.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: The first is on BO based on the FATF report, where information for Variable Capital Companies and unregistered foreign companies is not available in a timely manner or at all in certain cases.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: And hence, my question is will the central register's coverage be extended to these entities?

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: And if so, any timeline for doing so?

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: And the second question is in relation to the FATF report on the point that Singapore makes four times fewer Mutual Legal Assistance (MLA) requests than it receives, despite acknowledging that its primary risks lie abroad and that Singapore has sent a very modest number of MLAs to recover assets.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: So, my question is how does the Ministry intend to increase the use of MLAs or whether it is other formal or informal forms of cooperation channels, especially when it relates to scams?

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: For the second supplementary question, as it deals with enforcement measures, I will defer to the political appointment holder dealing with MHA matters.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: On the first one, our operational experience is that the law enforcement agencies can and have gotten timely and accurate BO information in relation to legal persons and legal arrangements.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: It may also help to appreciate that investigations do not start in a vacuum.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: Law enforcement agencies in Singapore work on leads which point them to relevant AML/CFT obligated entities to advance their investigations.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: We also tap on information in suspicious transaction reports as well as partnerships with the private sector and foreign partners.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: This has enabled us to get information in a timely manner.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: And also, there was no evidence that the BO information was inaccurate.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: We provided this evidence to the FATF assessors that we were able to get accurate BO information on unregistered foreign companies and legal arrangements in a timely manner as well.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: There is still a second supplementary question that has to be answered, Sir.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This applies not just to AML/CFT and PF, but also to scams.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: I have a supplementary question for Senior Minister of State on PF.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: It was pointed out in the FATF report that representatives of foreign flag states have a very low understanding of their PF obligations.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: And I think our own national risk assessment assessed that ship-to-ship transfers are quite a key vector – in a sense, a potential for PF to go through such routes.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: So, in terms of actions to be taken, it was stated that we will conduct more outreach to these entities.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: What else is the Government going to do about the maritime sector?

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: I am answering in my capacity as the Deputy Chairman of MAS.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: So, this is what the FATF was referring to, these representative offices of these foreign flag states based in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: And these would include the United Nations Security Council sanctions, which are given full effect in our domestic legislation.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: And any entity found to be in breach of our laws will be dealt with accordingly.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: The FATF has actually noted that Singapore has taken action against non-compliant entities.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Singapore has and will continue to engage these entities to alert them to the PF risks and also to remind them of their countering PF obligations.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: That is something we will continue to do.
